hero.title_html: Modular Go Libraries.<br class="hidden sm:inline">Every Workload.
hero.lead_html: Krewire is an end-to-end digital SDLC ecosystem — from the first line of the spec to production operations — built on three pillars: secure, sustainable, and scalable. From single-binary web monoliths to interactive TUIs, high-speed static sites, book pipelines, background workers, microservices, cloud infra, and Go WebAssembly runtimes — build everything in Go with one CLI kiw and zero JS fatigue.
hero.meta: Go 1.27.1+ · Spec to Production · File-based routing · Scoped CSS · 100% Zero JS by default

pillars.title: Secure. Sustainable. Scalable.
pillars.lead: Krewire is an end-to-end digital SDLC ecosystem — from the first line of the specification to running production. Every capability must pass all three pillars before it ships, and each claim traces to a spec, a test, or a gate.
pillars.secure_desc: Security is a default, not a feature. A stdlib-first dependency graph, secure-by-default HTTP primitives, OWASP/CWE-aligned controls, secrets referenced — never stored — and WASM sandboxing keep the attack surface small and auditable.
pillars.sustainable_desc: Software a single builder can still read, run, and afford a decade from now. Single static binaries with embedded assets, opt-in batteries that cost nothing when unused, boring proven parts, and no license fees — ever.
pillars.scalable_desc: Growth is additive, not a rewrite. The progressive pipeline takes a product from static site to monolith to workers, services, and infra — each stage an opt-in, reversible battery, from a $5 VPS to hyperscale.

workloads.title: Modular Libraries. Eight Workloads.
workloads.lead: Stop assembling disparate tools for web, CLI, background queues, and infra. Krewire provides unified ergonomics, shared configuration, and zero context switching.
workloads.app_desc: Fullstack web monolith — compile your web interface, HTTP routing, and API handlers into a single static Go binary.
workloads.cli_desc: Developer command-line tools & rich terminal interfaces powered by the lightweight TUI library with zero dependencies.
workloads.site_desc: High-performance static marketing sites, landing pages, and blogs built with the .kiw DSL and scoped CSS styling.
workloads.book_desc: Technical documentation, knowledge bases, and API references compiled with the standalone mdbind engine.
workloads.worker_desc: Asynchronous background queues, scheduled recurring tasks, and durable workers with graceful shutdowns.
workloads.service_desc: Headless microservices, JSON REST APIs, and gRPC endpoints engineered for high concurrency and low latency.
workloads.infra_desc: Automated bare-metal and VPS provisioning, TLS certificate issuance, and zero-downtime blue-green deployments.
workloads.runtime_desc: Reactive WebAssembly runtime compiling Go to client-side WASM with virtual DOM diffing and instant hot hydration.

steps.title: From Zero to Production in 4 Commands
steps.lead: No boilerplate scaffolding, no package manager wrestling, no hidden magic.
steps.s1_desc: Install the standalone kiw CLI tool via a single-line shell script or Go install.
steps.s2_desc: Generate a production-ready project template for any workload in under one second.
steps.s3_desc: Instant hot-reload local development server with file-based routing and scoped CSS updates.
steps.s4_desc: Compile into a single static binary or static asset bundle and ship to GitHub Pages or Docker.

why.title: Go-First. Progressive. Zero Bloat.
why.lead: Built for engineers who value compilation speed, predictable deployments, and maintainable software architecture.
why.w1_desc: No Node.js, no npm dependencies, and no bundler configuration. Your entire application compiles with standard Go tooling into clean, self-contained binaries.
why.w2_desc: Combines YAML frontmatter, standard Go HTML templates, and scoped <style> blocks. CSS classes never leak outside their component boundary.
why.w3_desc: Start as a lightweight static site, grow into a fullstack web monolith, then seamlessly extract background workers and microservices — all within the same ecosystem.
why.w4_desc: Engineered with production defaults: structured JSON logging, distributed tracing, health checks, circuit breakers, and graceful shutdown out of the box.

dsl.title: Write Pages as Clean .kiw Components
dsl.lead: The elegance of Svelte and Astro brought to Go. Frontmatter + HTML + scoped CSS in one intuitive file.
dsl.f1_html: Scoped by Default: Styles remain strictly isolated to the component.
dsl.f2_html: Global CSS via :root: Theme tokens cascade cleanly across layouts.
dsl.f3_html: Built into kiw: Compiled natively via kiw/dsl with zero npm or external bundler dependencies.
dsl.f4_html: Light & Dark Mode: Native token switching via data-theme.

matrix.title: Why Engineers Choose Krewire
matrix.lead: Compare the simplicity of an all-in-one Go toolchain against fragmented multi-language setups.
matrix.row6_trad: Heavy multi-stage Docker containers with Node layers
matrix.row6_krewire: Single self-contained Go binary or static assets

ecosystem.title: 4 Git Repositories — Unified Architecture
ecosystem.lead: The entire Krewire ecosystem is organized into exactly 4 focused repositories that compose cleanly.
ecosystem.core_desc: Core packages, apps, devtool CLI (kiw), and Boost agent templates in Go.
ecosystem.book_desc: Standalone Markdown book and docs site builder powering the book workload.
ecosystem.portal_desc: Official production website and documentation portal built with site kind & .kiw DSL.
ecosystem.community_desc: Community portal for contributors, releases, guides, and sponsorships.

cta.lead: Start with a lightweight static site, scale to a web monolith, then to distributed cloud services — one repository, one CLI, one configuration.
